hints.title: String Materialization Allocation Obstacle
hints.text: Building reconstructed strings requires allocating additional storage. How can reading both strings from right to left with backspace skip counters compare effective characters in O(1) space?

hints.title: Reverse Traversal Skip Invariant
hints.text: A backspace '#' only deletes characters to its left. Scanning backward allows counting how many characters must be skipped before encountering the next surviving character.

hints.title: Dual Backward Step Procedure
hints.text: Initialize pointers at the end of both strings. For each string, increment a skip counter when '#' is seen, and decrement skip while skipping normal characters until reaching an unskipped character. Compare the two characters; if unequal, return false. Return true when both finish.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of string s (1 <= N <= 200)
M: length of string t (1 <= M <= 200)
complexity.notes: Reverse two-pointer traversal avoids any string allocation.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Building output strings with string concatenation or arrays uses O(N + M) auxiliary memory.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Simulating backspaces in reverse achieves optimal O(1) auxiliary space without extra passes.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Implementing the O(1) space reverse pointer approach and handling edge cases like leading backspaces.
